corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'increase throughput by more than 20% and reduce memory usage by 60%' (LLaMA 3-8B, batch 8, bf16, AdamW, gradient checkpointing, FSDP1, 8 A100s; chart images); Hugging Face Trainer example 'Train LLaMA 3-8B ~20% faster with over 40% memory reduction' (4 A100s, FSDP); Lightning Trainer 15% throughput and 40% less memory (8 A100s, DeepSpeed ZeRO3); Medusa retraining 40% throughput and 80% less memory (8 A100s, FSDP). Kernel level, benchmark/data/all_benchmark_data.csv, full forward+backward median time ratio vs the huggingface provider (derived from page data): cross_entropy 2.40x to 2.87x, rms_norm 1.11x to 8.63x (median 4.56x), rope 1.88x to 10.24x (median 4.19x), but fused_linear_cross_entropy 0.46x to 0.89x (slower; it trades speed for memory), layer_norm 0.30x to 1.88x, group_norm 0.51x to 3.59x, embedding 0.72x to 1.27x. Versus the torch provider: softmax 0.08x to 1.81x (median 0.33x, i.e. mostly slower); versus torch_compile: embedding 0.50x to 0.80x (slower). README H100 table for the newer fused scaled cross-entropy (H=4096, V=131072, BF16): CuTe SM90 forward 3.12 ms vs Verl Torch fallback 11.36 ms at M=2048 (3.6x, derived from page data); B200 cuTile full 11.36 ms vs Torch 12.85 ms, backward slower (8.35 vs 7.15 ms).
corrections.caveats: End-to-end throughput charts are images; the end-to-end baseline is untuned eager Hugging Face (no torch.compile). The repo's own kernel benchmark data show many Liger kernels slower than the reference on some or most shapes: fused linear cross-entropy is 0.46x to 0.89x the speed of Hugging Face (its gain is memory), softmax is a median 0.33x of torch, embedding is slower than torch.compile, and layer_norm/group_norm drop to 0.30x/0.51x on some shapes. The QuACK (Dao-AILab) report of Liger softmax throughput falling from about 3.0 to 2.0 TB/s at large reduction dims on H100 was carried from the search record and not re-checked. No Triton/PyTorch versions or host CPU on the README. The baseline is not oneDNN/cuDNN/XNNPACK/Eigen.
